Using grid coordinates, let the vertical segment have endpoints  
\[
A=(0,1),\quad B=(0,3),
\]
and the horizontal segment have endpoints  
\[
C=(2,1),\quad D=(4,1).
\]
Also,
\[
T=(0,0),\quad U=(1,0),\quad V=(1,2),\quad W=(2,3).
\]

A rotation sending one segment to the other must map endpoints to endpoints. There are two possible endpoint matchings.

1. \(A\mapsto C\) and \(B\mapsto D\).  
   The center is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of \(AC\) and \(BD\), which is
   \[
   U=(1,0).
   \]

2. \(A\mapsto D\) and \(B\mapsto C\).  
   The center is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of \(AD\) and \(BC\), which is
   \[
   W=(2,3).
   \]

Thus exactly the points \(U\) and \(W\) can be centers of such a rotation.

\[
\boxed{\text{C: either }U\text{ and }W\text{ (both }U\text{ and }W\text{ can be centers)}}
\]
